question: Should OpenClaw’s first-class filesystem policy be a file-tool boundary only, or must it also provide an enforceable containment strategy for arbitrary shell execution before it is presented as sandboxing?
rationale: The answer determines the security claim, configuration shape, upgrade behavior, test matrix, and whether the related implementation is sufficient; source inspection cannot safely choose that product and security boundary.

options.title: File tools with explicit scope
options.body: Ship normalized deny-wins rules for file-oriented tools while documenting that arbitrary exec is outside this boundary and remains governed by the existing execution/sandbox controls.

options.title: Require shell containment
options.body: Do not expose the policy as filesystem sandboxing until the selected execution runtime can enforce the same host-path boundary for shell-mediated access.

options.title: Adopt sandbox isolation instead
options.body: Keep host filesystem policy narrow and direct security-sensitive deployments toward OS, container, or per-agent-account isolation rather than extending host tool permissions.

recommendation.title: File tools with explicit scope
recommendation.body: Ship normalized deny-wins rules for file-oriented tools while documenting that arbitrary exec is outside this boundary and remains governed by the existing execution/sandbox controls.
